interest: Reveals occupation debates rejecting imposed romanization or katakana in favor of Japanese self-determination and linguistic research.
overview: This file documents U.S. government evaluations, military proposals, and occupation policies concerning Japanese writing system reform between 1945 and 1949. It traces early wartime inquiries, military proposals urging the exclusive use of katakana, and State-War-Navy Coordinating Committee efforts to mandate romanization (Romaji). The records highlight the State Department's and General MacArthur's rejection of foreign directives in favor of Japanese domestic agency, culminating in the Japanese Diet's passage of Public Law No. 245 establishing the National Language Research Institute.
